claimed_purpose.text: ES-MemEval is a benchmark for evaluating conversational agents on personalized long-term emotional support tasks.

mechanisms.text: The QA task has five sub-categories: IE (Information Extraction), TR (Temporal Reasoning), CD (Contextual Dependency), Abs (Abstention), and UM (Understanding & Memory), with per-sub-category and aggregate scores reported.
The dialogue generation task also has a separate LLM-judge evaluation covering three dimensions: LT-Mem. (long-term memory), Pers. (personalization), and ES (emotional support).
The QA task evaluates answer prediction using F1 Score, BERTScore, and LLM-as-Judge (0–2 scale), across five question subtypes: IE, TR, CD, Abs, UM, plus an All aggregate.
Models evaluated include open-weight models served via vLLM (Mistral-Small-3.1-24B, Ministral-8B, Phi-3-medium-128k) and commercial APIs (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o).
The summarization task (exe/sum/) is evaluated with ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L, and event-based Precision/Recall/F1, plus an LLM Score on a 0–5 scale.
RAG retrieval is evaluated with Recall@k (R@k) and NDCG@k, at turn-level, round-level, and session-level granularities with varying top-k settings.
Benchmark is supported by EvoEmo, a multi-session dataset capturing fragmented, implicit user disclosures and evolving user states.
The benchmark uses a dataset called EvoEmo, stored at data/evo_emo.json, organized by seeker identifiers.
Context-length ablation for the QA task tests 2K, 4K, 8K, and 20K token windows.
